html:
Qataban was one of the ancient kingdoms of South Arabia, in today's Yemen, from the early first millennium BCE to the late 1st or 2nd century CE. Its capital was Timna in the Wadi Bayhan. The map shows it from 323 to 100 BCE.

It lay between Saba to the north and Hadramaut to the east, and like them it lived on farming with floodwater and on the incense trade. A long inscription at the gate of Timna sets out the city's trade laws. Its people wrote in the South Arabian alphabet and worshipped the moon god Amm.

For a time Qataban was strong enough to dominate its neighbours, but it lost ground as trade moved to the sea and new powers rose. It was taken over by Hadramaut, and its land later passed to the Himyarites.
